- opened gap-001 [partial] spec:"AC-12 The comma-separated format carries the same columns and
  values as the properties sheet"

  Evidence: `export/text.py` `for_delimited` against `export/text.py` `for_cell`, and
  `tests/test_export_safety.py`.

  Literally true for every value except one shape, and deliberately so. A spreadsheet cell carries a
  type, and forcing it to text changes nothing about the value. A comma-separated file has no types,
  so the only thing available to say "read what follows as text" is a leading apostrophe, which is a
  different value by one character.

  For a cell whose first non-whitespace character is `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`, AC-12 and the security
  requirement in the same document cannot both be literally satisfied. The pre-build check raised it
  as B-2 rather than leaving it to whoever wrote the test first, because an equality assertion
  passes by dropping the guard and a guard passes by weakening the assertion, and either way
  somebody makes a security decision without noticing.

  Settled as: the same columns, the same values, with each format's own protection applied. The
  equality test compares the two formats over ordinary values and passes; the guard is asserted
  separately in each. It fires for none of the 263 real descriptions this project has measured.

  Routed: a human decision, and the recommendation is to legitimize it as a clause on AC-12 rather
  than remove the guard. Recorded, not self-applied.

- opened gap-002 [unrequested] code:"columns beyond the default set"

  Evidence: `export/columns.py` `COLUMNS`, the entries below the comment marking where the default
  set ends: `Wildfire Hazard`, `Elevation (ft)`, `Notes`, `Flags`, `Sources`, `Description`,
  `Listing ID`, `First Seen`.

  Eight columns the spec never asks for. They exist because AC-7 makes templates configuration and a
  template can only name a column that exists, so a configurable column set with nothing outside the
  default in it is configurable in one direction only. Every one of them is a value this tool already
  holds and already shows somewhere else.

  Two of them are the pre-build check's S-2 landing here. Wildfire hazard and elevation bear directly
  on the default sheet's `Fire/Egress/Terrain` column, and the first draft of the plan proposed
  filling it from them. That was refused: `Fire/Egress/Terrain` is a column the person writes notes
  in, and a machine's summary in a notes column replaces their work with an opinion nobody asked for.
  The values are offered as their own columns instead, and the default set does not include them.

  Routed: a human decision. The recommendation is to legitimize them as an addition to AC-7, whose
  "adding or reordering columns requires no code change" is only meaningfully true if there is
  something to add. Recorded, not self-applied.

## What was checked and found clean

- **AC-1 is checked against the specification rather than against the code.** The pre-build check's
  first Blocking finding was that the column list it measures against lived in a discovery document
  at the repository root and not in any spec artifact, which made the required test a comparison
  between the implementation and itself. `spec.md` now carries the thirty-two names, and
  `test_export_columns.py` parses them out of it and compares them to the header row of a file it
  wrote.
- **Nothing this writes will be evaluated, and that is checked in the file rather than in memory.**
  Every text cell has its type forced without exception, and the test opens the saved archive and
  asserts that the sheet's XML contains no formula element at all. Eight hostile values are written,
  including `=cmd|'/c calc'!A1` and a leading-whitespace variant, in both formats.
- **The library's two silent behaviours are handled before it sees the value.** It truncates a cell
  past 32,767 characters without an error, so the truncation happens first and leaves a visible
  mark; and it raises on a control character, which would cost a whole workbook over one bad byte in
  one listing, so they are removed. Both were found by probing rather than by reading documentation.
- **Export writes nothing to the store, and it is checked against every table.** Not a spot check of
  annotations: a hash of every row of every table in the database, before and after, including the
  paths a person actually takes (both formats, a custom template, `--include-dropped`, `--force`)
  and the paths that fail.
- **There is no import path, and that is checked in the source.** A scan of the package for anything
  that reads a workbook, and for any file opened in a mode that is not a write, using the same
  technique the source adapters use to prove they carry no credential. A behavioural test cannot
  notice a reader nothing calls yet, and a reader nothing calls yet is exactly how this rule breaks.
- **A source-supplied URL is checked before it becomes a hyperlink.** `http` and `https` only. A
  `file://` target in a spreadsheet is not a broken link, it is a request to whatever path it names,
  and a property whose link is refused is written as plain text rather than as a link to nowhere,
  which is also the spec's own edge case for a property with no link at all.
- **Product invariant 10 arrives intact at the last surface that could break it.** An undetermined
  value is an empty cell with no placeholder and no default, a property with no price has no price
  per square foot rather than a zero that sorts to the top, and the five structurally empty columns
  are empty on purpose.
- **The empty columns are explained rather than left to be guessed at.** Eleven of the thirty-two
  come out blank on a fresh store for three unrelated reasons, and the export says which is which:
  run the enrichment pass, write some notes, or nothing fills this. Measured on a live run over
  Portales, where it printed exactly that.
- **Five thousand properties export in under four seconds**, against a thirty-second budget, because
  annotations, verdicts, enriched values and cached extractions are each gathered in one pass rather
  than per property per column.
- **A failure leaves nothing behind.** The file is built in memory, written beside its destination
  and moved into place. A directory where a file was wanted leaves neither a partial file nor a
  changed database, and the Windows case the spec names, the file being open in Excel, is reported
  as itself.
